title: Shareholding limit on banks and insurers
summary: The Financial Sector (Shareholdings) Act 1998 bars any person from holding more than 20% of a financial sector company without the Treasurer's approval.
direction_rationale: A limit on large stakes, lifted only with the Treasurer's approval, restricts who may own financial institutions.

verified.notes: An existing setting: no dates. The requirement inside it quotes s 11.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 17 November 2026 (phase 6 of the levers re-evaluation, batch 1) from the law quoted. Not yet checked: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: No one may hold more than 20% of a bank, insurer or their holding company without the Treasurer's approval. It makes takeovers of financial institutions harder, which shelters incumbents from the discipline of a takeover.

marks.reason: An approval hurdle on large stakes in financial institutions.
Weakens the threat of takeover that disciplines incumbent managers.

assessment.confidence_note: The limit and its approval route are explicit; the four pillars policy is applied through it.
